about: One owning module for every engine capability (OWN.1, user decision 2026-10-26), beside the module registry (the crd_module lines of the root CMakeLists.txt). status: landed (the owner is registered and its public API exists), assigned (the owner is registered; the named row creates its API there) or planned (the named row creates the owner module). A signature found in engine/ outside the owner is a second implementation: scripts/check-capability-owners.py (the crd-check-capability-owners CTest and repository step) fails on it unless the file is pending (its row moves it onto the owner) or allowed (with the reason). docs/design/capability-ownership.md.

capabilities.summary: CPUID, XGETBV and the OS feature queries: the one reading of the CPU's features, OS-enabled state, hybrid cores and the forced level (ADR-0134), and of its identity: vendor, model, signature and microcode (HW-RESILIENCE.2).

signatures.what: a CPU or OS feature query

capabilities.summary: Per-level kernel units and their runtime selection: the level macros, the kernel tables and the process level (ADR-0134); each kernel family lives in its owning module and reaches its level through these.

signatures.what: a compiler ISA macro read outside the kernel-level header

capabilities.summary: Search folding of Unicode text one code point at a time: letters lower case, Latin diacritics, ligatures and fullwidth forms to ASCII (the Turkish dotted and dotless i to i), Greek and Cyrillic without case or accents, combining marks and apostrophes elided, punctuation and spaces as separators, from the table scripts/gen-text-fold.py derives from the Unicode Character Database; and the UTF-8 decoding it reads.
capabilities.decision: crd-core, beside its UTF-8 well-formedness rule: dependency-free and allocation-free, so name screening (crd-comply) and every later search, sort key or identifier comparison folds text one way. docs/design/registers.md#screening.

capabilities.summary: UTF-16 decoding and encoding and the transcoding between UTF-16 and UTF-8 into caller storage, an unpaired surrogate and a byte that starts no UTF-8 sequence read as U+FFFD: every crossing between the engine's UTF-8 text and Windows' UTF-16 (paths, module and adapter names, the environment, the command line) and the UTF-16 a minidump holds.
capabilities.decision: crd-core, beside the UTF-8 rule it shares: header-only, constexpr and allocation-free, so the environment reader before main, the crash path and every module transcode one way, and the Linux lanes test what Windows runs. COMPLY.1, docs/sessions/2026-11-01-utf8-arguments-and-environment.md.

capabilities.summary: The program's command-line arguments as UTF-8 on every platform: on Windows the UTF-16 command line split by the Microsoft C runtime's rules and transcoded, never the ANSI code page's argv or its best-fit mapping; on POSIX main's argv in place.

signatures.what: a read of the process's command line

capabilities.decision: crd-platform, the process's boundary with its OS: every tool's main and the sandbox read their arguments through it, so a Turkish name or a fullwidth quote reaches a verb as it was passed. COMPLY.1, docs/sessions/2026-11-01-utf8-arguments-and-environment.md.

capabilities.summary: FNV-1a hashing, 32- and 64-bit, over bytes and text (constant-expression capable), little-endian integer folds and the runtime word step: identities, cache keys and cooked-content hashes.
capabilities.decision: crd-core, not crd-containers: crd-memory (below containers) hashes allocation stacks with it, and crd-core already holds the other dependency-free integer primitives (wide_multiply, the seed generators). crd-containers re-exports fnv1a_64 for its hash_string.

allowed.why: A per-light seed stride baked into a generated device hash (with xxHash32 constants); not FNV-1a, and the device program carries its own copy by design.

capabilities.summary: The golden-ratio hash combiner (seed ^= v + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 + (seed << 6) + (seed >> 2)) that folds already-hashed words into one key.
capabilities.decision: Beside FNV-1a in crd/core/fnv1a.hpp (design decision 7): both fold words into runtime and cooked keys.

capabilities.summary: CRC-32 (ISO-HDLC) and CRC-32C, one dispatched family with its carry-less-multiply and CRC-instruction levels (HW-RESILIENCE.1).
XXH3-64, seeded, dispatched across its vector levels (HW-RESILIENCE.1).

SplitMix64 and the 64-bit MMIX linear congruential step: the integer generators that seed engines, fault plans, workload probes and the starting vectors of iterative methods, below every module that uses them.
capabilities.decision: Foundation modules (core's workload probe, perf's fault injection, the CEIR input generator) cannot reach hesap-stats, so the step functions live in crd-core; hesap-stats' SplitMix64 and PCG engines build on them.

capabilities.summary: Pseudo- and quasi-random engines (xoshiro256, PCG64, SFC64, Philox, Threefry, ChaCha, MT19937, QMC sequences) and every distribution and sampler built on them.
Sorting and selection over engine containers (the standard algorithms stay banned, check_no_std_sort).
Big-endian integers over byte spans: the bounded writer and reader of every Cerid wire and signed artefact layout.
Arrays, hash maps and sets, rings, queues, slot maps, strings and spans (the standard containers stay banned, check_no_std_containers).
Allocators, arenas, pools, the diagnostic allocator and memory statistics.
The fiber job system, parallel ranges and frame arenas.
File-system access, asynchronous file I/O, file watching and dynamic libraries.

signatures.what: a directory walk or a file attribute read by hand

allowed.why: The crash handler's install confirms its output directory with the OS's own call: crd-core sits below crd-platform, and the crash-time writer uses only calls safe in a crashed process.
Counts the process's open descriptors through /proc/self/fd to judge an OS object's presence, a process probe rather than file access; crd-core sits below crd-platform.

capabilities.summary: The machine a diagnostic bundle was written on: firmware and board, memory and its modules from the SMBIOS table, the GPUs and drivers, with the CPU identity from cpu.detection (HW-RESILIENCE.2).

signatures.what: a firmware table or DMI read

capabilities.summary: Hardware fault classification: a native crash capture's fault and the faulting thread's registers read from a minidump or a crash record, its impossible-state signatures (machine checks, one-bit code and data address flips, replays that do not reproduce, a one-bit difference between the faulting instruction's bytes and its module's image, a fault on an access the decoded instruction does not make, a divide error its operands cannot raise), the known-unstable processor table and the user's sentence (HW-RESILIENCE.2).

State-hash ledgers of deterministic runs (per-step XXH3-64 hashes and their chain, bounded, with their payload) and the divergence check: the first divergent step against a reference or the majority, and the diverging machine named by its hardware identity; the ledger as a flight-bundle section and the state.divergence command over a directory of bundles (HW-RESILIENCE.3).
Durable saves: the atomic, flushed replace of a file, generational checksummed saves with their fallback, the checksummed journal and the autosave cadence (HW-RESILIENCE.1).

signatures.what: a durable replace or flush of a file

capabilities.decision: crd-platform owns durable files with the rest of file I/O. crd-perf's bundle publish (write_bundle_atomic) is its atomic replace since 2026-11-01, when crd-platform joined the relocatable package (decision 9: its window backend split into crd-platform-window).

capabilities.summary: The window backend: the GLFW runtime (PlatformContext) and OS windows that feed crd-platform's input snapshot.

signatures.what: the window backend's runtime or a window created by hand

capabilities.decision: Split from crd-platform on 2026-11-01 (decision 9) so the OS boundary links no window library and joins the relocatable package; headers and namespace are unchanged.

capabilities.summary: Log channels, records, levels and sinks.
Clocks, durations, deadlines, deterministic and rational time.
Dimensioned quantities and unit conversion.
TOML parsing for authored configuration.
Lossless compression codecs: raw DEFLATE and inflate, the zstd binding with trained dictionaries, and the GDeflate CPU paths of the crdr v2 chunks.

signatures.what: a direct zstd call or include

capabilities.decision: Compression belongs to a foundation module unless a decision records otherwise (OWN.1; the publishing research's P-4 asks): crd-perf's bundle refused compressed sections only because the codec sat in crd-resources, above it. OWN.1 created crd-compression (2026-10-31) and moved resources' raw DEFLATE, inflate, zlib and Adler-32 and its zstd binding there (zstd's header is private to it); resources, its CRDR container and shader-cook through it consume it, hesap-tensor's npz inflate merged with it into one exact-size decoder (2026-11-01), perf's bundle compresses its sections through it (2026-11-01: raw DEFLATE, bounded exact-size decoding), the module and the pinned zstd archive ship in the relocatable package, and SHIP.2's crdr v2 chunk codecs (trained dictionaries, GDeflate) land in it.

capabilities.summary: The ZIP (PKZIP APPNOTE) container: the end-of-central-directory search (Zip64 included), the central directory and local headers, STORED and DEFLATE members extracted with their CRC-32 and size checked, and an archive written with its central directory.
capabilities.decision: Two ZIP containers existed: resources' ZipReader and ZipWriter (3MF and the cooker; Zip64 read, DEFLATE written) and hesap-tensor's npz reader and writer (STORED written, as np.savez does). hesap-tensor sits below crd-resources, so the one container could not live there; it is a container of compressed members over the codecs, so it moved into crd-compression (decision 8 of docs/design/capability-ownership.md, 2026-11-01): its writer takes each member's method, its reader keeps STORED members as views of the source and decodes either method into an exact-size buffer, and the cooker, ceridc's import and hesap-tensor's npz reader and writer consume it.

capabilities.summary: Fixed-size vector, matrix and quaternion types and their closed-form operations: 2x2 and 3x3 determinants, inverses, the inverse-transpose and Cramer solves, and the 4x4 inverse.

allowed.why: CKIR's CUDA emitter writes the determinant into generated device source; the host routine is crd-math's.

capabilities.summary: Deterministic transcendental and elementary scalar functions and their SIMD forms (check_no_std_math, check_no_std_transcendental).
Adaptive exact orientation, in-circle and in-sphere predicates (Shewchuk).
Spatial indices and their queries: k-d trees, octrees, R-trees, uniform grids, spatial hashes.
Bounding-volume hierarchies: build, refit, ray, overlap and shape-cast queries.
Convex hulls, GJK, EPA, SAT and convex shape casts.
Delaunay triangulation and tetrahedralization, Voronoi diagrams, Lloyd relaxation and Delaunay refinement.
Polygon booleans, constrained triangulation, segment intersection and polygon predicates.
Mesh repair, decimation, remeshing, smoothing, subdivision, meshlets and cluster DAGs.
Parametric curves: Bezier, B-spline, Catmull-Rom, Hermite, arcs, arc length and frames.
Voxelization and approximate convex decomposition.
Analysis meshing for simulation: surface and tetrahedral meshing, size fields and quality metrics.
Dense BLAS, LU, QR, Cholesky, LDLT, SVD and the dense symmetric and nonsymmetric eigenproblems.
Sparse storage formats, conversions, sparse kernels and Matrix Market I/O.
Sparse direct factorizations and solves (supernodal and multifrontal LU, LDLT, Cholesky, low-rank compression).
Krylov solvers: CG and preconditioned CG, GMRES, BiCGStab, IDR(s), GCR and their block forms.
Jacobi, block-Jacobi, incomplete factorizations, sparse approximate inverses and polynomial preconditioners.
Algebraic multigrid: strength, coarsening, interpolation and cycles.
Fill-reducing and bandwidth orderings and symbolic analysis.
Sparse and iterative eigensolvers and partial SVD (Lanczos, Arnoldi, Krylov-Schur, LOBPCG, Jacobi-Davidson, FEAST).
Unconstrained, constrained, derivative-free and global optimization, QP, conic and KKT solvers.
Linear complementarity and box-constrained mixed LCP solves (projected Gauss-Seidel and its successors): the numerical core of contact and joint constraint solving.
capabilities.decision: No eylem constraint solver exists yet (eylem ships data descriptors and a null scene). Eylem owns contact generation, constraint rows and their Jacobians; the solve itself is a hesap-opt capability that EYLEM-v1e's Sequential Impulses solver creates there and EYLEM-v1f's joints reuse.

capabilities.summary: ODE and DAE integration: explicit, implicit, IMEX and BDF steppers, step control, dense output and events.
Complex, real, multidimensional, non-uniform and sparse Fourier transforms and the DCT.
Discrete, stationary, packet and continuous wavelet transforms and denoising.
Digital signal processing, audio DSP included: filter design and filtering, convolution, spectral estimation, multirate and adaptive filters.

signatures.what: a biquad's direct-form II transposed state update

capabilities.decision: The section step (biquad_step, beside Biquad and BiquadState in filter.hpp) is the engine's one DF2T recurrence: sosfilt_stream cascades it and the audio module's apply_biquad runs it per channel (OWN.1, 2026-10-31).

capabilities.summary: Perceptual image metrics for golden tests (HDR-FLIP and a ColorVideoVDP-class metric) and their difference maps.
capabilities.decision: OWN.1 takes IMG-ORACLE's recommendation: a crd-hesap module beside hesap-dsp, on hesap-fft and hesap-stats; tooling owns no numerics.

capabilities.summary: Special functions: gamma, Bessel, Airy, elliptic, error and exponential integrals.
Numerical integration: Gauss rules, adaptive and oscillatory quadrature, cubature.
Descriptive, robust and streaming statistics, hypothesis tests, regression, resampling, density estimation and MCMC.
Interpolation and splines: piecewise, cubic and Akima splines, rational, barycentric, RBF, kriging, gridded and keyframe interpolation.
Finite-difference, complex-step, spectral and Savitzky-Golay differentiation.
Automatic differentiation: forward dual numbers, reverse tapes, sparse Jacobians and Hessians.
Dense tensors, einsum, batched and elementwise operations, DLPack exchange and tensor I/O.
Trajectory and motion profiles: online trajectory generation, polynomial trajectories, clothoids, NURBS paths and rotation splines.
Digital communications: modulation, pulse shaping, framing, equalization, timing and carrier recovery, OFDM.
The finite-element core: function spaces, assembly, boundary conditions and hp-adaptivity, solving through hesap.
The finite-volume core: polyhedral cells, fluxes, reconstruction, limiters and pressure-velocity coupling, solving through hesap.
Reduced-coordinate articulations and robot-description import (URDF, MJCF, USD physics), with forward and inverse kinematics.
Aerodynamic forces, the standard atmosphere and propulsion for flight models.

Sockets, transport, sessions, channels, bounded admission, wire negotiation with GREASE, link conditioning, NAT traversal, the client side of relays and capture: no other module opens a socket (network foundation D1).
capabilities.decision: docs/design/network-foundation.md D1: one owner for every path that can reach another machine. NET-STD's negotiation codec created the module (2026-10-31); 4.2a adds the transport.

capabilities.summary: Algorithm identifiers generated from the NET-STD standards register, the signature verification interface providers implement and signed, monotonic crypto policy generations with dated windows, an offline grace period and the build's ceiling.
capabilities.decision: docs/design/network-foundation.md D2 and D7: NET-STD's policy generations created the module (2026-10-31); every signed artefact names its algorithms by register identifier and verifies through the interface, never a provider's own constant.

capabilities.summary: The cryptographic provider interface (AEAD, KEM, signatures, KDF, keyed PRF), the operating-system CSPRNG, the key store and the TLS and QUIC handshake integration over vetted providers; Cerid writes no primitive (network foundation D2).

signatures.what: a cryptographic library or operating-system randomness header
an operating-system or library randomness call

capabilities.decision: docs/design/network-foundation.md D2: its consumers are wider than the network (SUPPLY signing, policy and rule generations, crash pack protection), so cryptography is a foundation owner that depends on no network code. NET-STD created the module; NET.2 landed the provider interface over the pinned AWS-LC (2026-11-01: randomness, AEAD, HKDF, signatures, key agreement, then the ML-KEM key encapsulation and the SipHash-2-4 keyed PRF for tables; docs/design/network-foundation.md#provider), then TLS 1.3 sessions over its TLS stack with the hybrid groups (2026-11-01, #tls-sessions), and its later slices add the key store and the QUIC handshake integration to the same owner.

capabilities.summary: Authority over sessions: signed, attenuating, session-bound capability tokens and revocation generations, the message schemas an audience's issuers authorize with the operation verdict (declared, granted and, as early data, idempotent), and the anti-replay windows and single-use filters (network foundation S15 to S18).
capabilities.decision: docs/design/network-foundation.md D5: authentication and authorisation are separate stages and 0-RTT carries only schema-declared idempotent operations. NET.2 landed the capability tokens (2026-11-02, #capability-tokens), the anti-replay windows and filters (#anti-replay) and the message schemas (#message-schemas) in crd-crypto, so admission (NET.3's stages S6 and S7) and the session layer (4.2a) call them and never re-implement a token, schema or replay check.

capabilities.summary: End-to-end group keys: hybrid public key encryption (RFC 9180 base mode over the provider's primitives) and the Messaging Layer Security protocol (RFC 9420: cipher suites, the presentation language, tree math, the labelled operations and, as NET.2 lands them, the secret tree, key schedule, framing, ratchet tree, commits and Welcome), whose relays and delivery servers see only ciphertext (threat T14).
capabilities.decision: docs/design/network-foundation.md H1 and M1 to M7: NET.2 landed HPKE and MLS's first layers, its key schedule and secret tree, its message framing and protection (mls_message.hpp) and its ratchet tree and TreeKEM (mls_tree.hpp) in crd-crypto (2026-11-02, #hpke, #mls), so calls' SFrame keys (NET-LIVE) and shared projects' end-to-end sessions (COLLAB.1) derive from one MLS group implementation and never carry their own.

capabilities.summary: The bidirectional ROS 2 topic and service bridge over crd-net.
Geometric path planning: A*, RRT and RRT*, PRM and lattice motion primitives; trajectory optimization stays numerics.optimization (CONTROL.8).
2D and 3D plotting for tools, notebooks and CHIR scripts.
Publishing: profiles, target descriptors, cook orchestration, package assembly, signing orchestration, store adapters, entitlements and the updater.
The Cerid store services and client library; it consumes crd-ship and owns no entitlement, payment, updater or store-adapter code.

Legal and platform obligations: the reviewed rule generations scripts/gen-comply-rules.py writes per jurisdiction from the COMPLY.0 legal register, decoded whole and swapped live by RuleStore, the query of the rules that bind a scope on a day (proven or unproven) served by ceridc comply and, after MCP-ADAPT, by MCP; sanctions and embargo screening (COMPLY.1): each authority's list as a cerid-sanctions/1 generation swapped live by SanctionsStore, the name matcher and the fail-closed screening of parties and destinations, served by ceridc screen; and the checks and shared generators (data inventory, notices, classification records, store answers) the governed rows consume.

signatures.what: a Jaro-Winkler name similarity (the screening matcher is crd-comply's names.hpp)

capabilities.decision: docs/design/registers.md#rule-generations and #screening: the JSON register is the guarded source of truth and every jurisdiction's generation is reviewed before it ships (its digest recorded in the register); COMPLY owns rules, checks, screening and generators, the governed rows (the STORE rows for accounts and payments) consume them and write no second rule engine or matcher.
